newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks rebound after Monday's sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks rebound after Monday's sell-off.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose Tuesday as the market enjoyed a bounce following the previous day's sell-off, which was fuelled by a drop in technology shares.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 15.78 at 6,822.32, recovering from Monday's tumble of nearly 50 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on volume of about 260 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"Today is another display of resilience by the market as the common wisdom seems to be to buy on any setback," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
"But we are having trouble surmounting the 6,900 barrier on the Dow. It looks like that is the high end of the range for the time being."
High technology stocks, however, saw only a modest rebound as momentum players looked elsewhere for stock values.

"The rebound in the high techs isn't terribly convincing after Monday's bloodbath," Metz said. "The momentum players will have to go shop somewhere else for their vehicles, or victims, depending on how you look at it.

"I think that the likeliest candidates are consumer non-durables like drugs and tobacco. The message of the techs seems to be that margins are under pressure. I fear this may be the experience of other sectors of the economy."
Metz said the companies' profit margins were being squeeze due to a strong dollar, weak overseas demand and rising wage costs. A stronger dollar makes U.S. goods more expensive overseas.
The catalyst for Monday's market slide was a profit warning from 3Com Corp., which triggered a sell-off of 13-1/2, or more than a quarter, in the company's stock to 37-1/4.
On Tuesday, 3Com rallied 7/8 to 38-1/8. It was the most actively traded Nasdaq issue. Also active were, Cisco Systems Inc., which rose 2-3/8 to 60-3/8 and Intel Corp. up 1 at 152-5/8.
Others fared less well. U.S. Robotics Corp. was down 3-7/16 at 58-71/6, Applied Materials was down 1-1/2 at 45 and Ascend Communications fell 4-1/2 to 58-1/8.
Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. said the market has been undergoing a mood change for the past two weeks.
"We have finished fourth quarter earnings, and the focus is on the first and second quarters of this year. There we have deepening worries," he said.

"This occurs at a time when the market is overvalued. In my opinion, all the returns that portfolio managers thought they would get this year, they got in January. Everybody is surprised. It has moved the stock market in January to levels we did not think it would hit until year's end."
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 4.10 points to 1,331.24, while the American Stock Exchange index was up 1.16 at 589.00.
